subject.title: Support profile-qualified agent-to-agent routing for separate gateway profiles

question: Should OpenClaw make authenticated cross-profile gateway routing a first-class core capability, expose a narrow plugin seam for it, or keep separate profiles intentionally isolated?
rationale: The limitation is real, but changing it expands the gateway trust model and requires product ownership of peer discovery, credentials, authorization, provenance, and failure behavior.

options.title: Design core peer routing
options.body: Define explicit configured gateway peers, authentication, per-agent authorization, provenance, and typed failure behavior before implementation.

options.title: Expose a plugin seam
options.body: Add only the minimum stable SDK or gateway protocol surface needed for an external routing plugin to own peer discovery and delivery.

options.title: Keep profiles isolated
options.body: Document the existing CLI or external-orchestrator workflow and state that session tools remain scoped to one gateway profile.

recommendation.title: Design core peer routing
recommendation.body: Define explicit configured gateway peers, authentication, per-agent authorization, provenance, and typed failure behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest combined history signal spans inter-session provenance, core session behavior, gateway connectivity, and security-sensitive routing decisions.
